- **self**: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting (19/8)

## Structure and components

- [statement] Bitsgap’s accounting explainer identifies funding costs as an additional component for leveraged futures positions. It also warns that other bots and manual trades on the same account can affect overall balance; account-level changes therefore require attribution before they describe one bot’s result. (low confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/why-your-trading-bot-shows-profit-but-you-still-lose-money-quick-answer · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting

## How it works

- [statement] GIPS describes time-weighted returns as attempting to neutralize external cash flows. For its applicable composite portfolios, it requires sub-period returns at large cash flows when daily returns are unavailable and geometric linking of periodic and sub-period returns. This provides a cash-flow-aware methodology reference, without establishing GIPS compliance for a bot monitor. (low confidence) — https://www.gipsstandards.org/standards/gips-standards-for-firms/gips-standards-handbook-for-firms/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] The Hummingbot issue reporter described zero Trade P&L after trades in release 1.0.0; commenters reported only fees appearing. This is historical user-reported evidence that a displayed zero can reflect a measurement problem, without establishing a current bug or a confirmed root cause. (low confidence) — https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/5069 · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] In a Freqtrade issue discussion, maintainer xmatthias warns that market orders can slip and that estimated exit fees use the entry fee as a template, which can differ when entry and exit order types differ. This scopes estimated pre-exit profit; it does not establish a current unresolved accounting bug. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/12000 · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Kraken ledger evidence distinguishes trade, deposit, withdrawal, and transfer entry types. Its response example includes a reference ID, time, asset, amount, fee, and balance; retain this distinction when reconciling bot results against exchange funds movements. (low confidence) — https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/rest-api/get-ledgers-info/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In the same Freqtrade discussion, the reporter later acknowledged a dynamic stoploss calculation error that could close a position below the expected price and was at least partly responsible for the observed discrepancy. The original report should therefore not be presented as proof that the bot profit calculation was defective. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/12000 · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] GIPS requires both gross-of-fees and net-of-fees returns to deduct transaction costs. In GIPS terminology, net-of-fees returns also deduct investment management fees. A bot monitor borrowing these labels should disclose its cost scope rather than assume all products use identical definitions. (low confidence) — https://www.gipsstandards.org/standards/gips-standards-for-firms/gips-standards-handbook-for-firms/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Methodology inference: monitor both realized and unrealized profit and disclose included costs instead of treating a positive realized-profit display as sufficient evidence of positive total performance. Freqtrade explicitly combines realized and unrealized profit; the Coinmonks author reports test bots with positive reported gains that omitted changing position value. (medium confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting · also: https://medium.com/coinmonks/grid-bots-how-they-really-work-how-to-make-money-with-them-948b4439fa5f
- [statement] A historical Freqtrade issue challenges doubling a fee rate instead of calculating entry and exit fees against their respective transaction values. Treat this as a historical accounting failure mode, rather than evidence of a current Freqtrade defect. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/176 · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Hummingbot’s documented history calculation measures trade P&L against a hold portfolio valued at the current market price, rather than simply comparing ending equity to starting cash. Its sample records fees as negative, so adding the signed Fees paid term reduces Total P&L. Preserve the benchmark and fee sign when consuming these fields. (low confidence) — https://hummingbot.org/client/history · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Freqtrade documents exchange default fees for backtest, hyperopt, and dry-run calculations, but exchange-applied fees including rebates for live operation. A monitor comparing results across these modes should record the fee basis rather than assume identical net-cost treatment. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Freqtrade defines current profit as unrealized profit, realized profit as relevant to partial exits, and total profit as their combination; its profit calculations include fees. These are Freqtrade-specific definitions. (low confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Hummingbot documents Trade P&L as current portfolio value minus the hold portfolio value, with starting inventory valued at the current market price. It documents total P&L as trade P&L plus signed fees paid and return as total P&L divided by hold portfolio value. This is a hold-relative measure. (low confidence) — https://hummingbot.org/client/history · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Kraken Get Ledgers Info distinguishes trade, deposit, withdrawal, transfer, margin, adjustment and rollover ledger types, among others. Its response example separates asset, amount, fee and balance. Monitor reconciliation can use this separation to classify external funds movements independently from trading activity; the endpoint alone does not define a portfolio return. (low confidence) — https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/rest-api/get-ledgers-info/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Positive completed-grid profit does not establish positive overall bot performance: total P&L also includes unrealized inventory gains or losses, which can outweigh realized gains. (high confidence) — https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/FAQ-Spot-Grid-Bot · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/why-your-trading-bot-shows-profit-but-you-still-lose-money-quick-answer
- [statement] Include transaction costs in measured performance. Freqtrade documents fee-inclusive profit calculations; GIPS requires transaction costs to be deducted from both gross-of-fees and net-of-fees returns in its reporting framework. (high confidence) — https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/ · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting · also: https://www.gipsstandards.org/standards/gips-standards-for-firms/gips-standards-handbook-for-firms/
- [statement] Separate external funding movements from trading results. OKX defines Total PnL using live-marked bot equity relative to initial equity with top-ups and withdrawals accounted for; Bitsgap identifies deposits and withdrawals as balance changes unrelated to trading. (high confidence) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/how-do-total-profit-and-loss-pnl-and-grid-profits-work · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/why-your-trading-bot-shows-profit-but-you-still-lose-money-quick-answer
- [statement] OKX describes Grid Profits and Unpaired PnL as display-only estimates. Its grid-profit estimate excludes unrealized positions, Earn interest, and trading fees not tied to grid execution; rounding, fee currencies, and normalized quantities can make the breakdown approximate. (low confidence) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/how-do-total-profit-and-loss-pnl-and-grid-profits-work · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting
- [statement] Do not equate cumulative grid profit with immediately withdrawable cash. Bybit may retain profits for holding costs, while OKX describes prior withdrawals, reinvestment, fee approximations, rounding, and minimum trade sizes as constraints on the withdrawable amount. (high confidence) — https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/FAQ-Spot-Grid-Bot · keywords: Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting · also: https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/how-do-total-profit-and-loss-pnl-and-grid-profits-work

## Research summary — Crypto bot net performance and cash-flow accounting

Bot accounting needs explicit profit and cost definitions. Freqtrade combines realized and unrealized profit and includes fees; Hummingbot documents performance relative to a hold portfolio. GIPS supplies a reference for separating external cash-flow effects from investment performance. Kraken ledger records distinguish funds movements from trades. Historical issue discussions and a grid-bot critique show why monitor figures need reconciliation and why a reported discrepancy must retain its attribution and scope.
